title: How creator payouts differ from contractor payroll
summary: Infinite runs creator payouts as a variable batch and contractor payroll as a repeating pay-run, two operations that can share rails.

TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Creator payouts are a batch of earnings; contractor payroll is a repeating roster pay-run.
2. Recipients in both cases should be reviewed before the first payment, then screened again on every instruction.
3. Creator amounts and destinations often change from run to run; payroll is usually more stable.
4. A failed creator payout should not hold up the rest of the batch.
5. Local rails or stablecoins can serve either run, chosen per corridor.


01


## What is different about the recipient?


A creator is paid because they earned on a platform: revenue share, tips, sponsorships, or bonuses. The roster can grow quickly, and many recipients will be paid only when they have a balance to send. A contractor is paid because they work for the company on a schedule. The roster is smaller, more stable, and usually known before the pay period starts.


[Global creator payouts](https://infinite.net/industries/creator-economy) is the product page for the first pattern.[Paying global contractors in stablecoins](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/insights/paying-global-contractors-in-stablecoins) is the essay for the second. This page is only the distinction: what changes in the run when the recipient is a creator rather than a contractor.


Both still start as counterparties. Each person is reviewed before the first payout, and each instruction is screened again before funds move. The difference is not that one group can skip review.


02


## How does the run itself differ?


Creator payouts Contractor payroll


Cadence Often after earnings land, sometimes more than once a pay period A regular pay-run to a roster


Amounts Change with earnings, tips, or bonuses Usually set by contract or hours


Destinations Can be a local account or a stablecoin, and may change Usually a standing destination


Failure One failed payout should leave the rest of the run intact A failed salary still has to be resolved before the next cycle


Record One report should close the whole batch across corridors One report should close the pay period


A creator run is closer to a[marketplace payout](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/insights/marketplace-payouts) than to payroll: the seller experience is the product, and a delay or a short landing amount shows up as a trust problem. Payroll is a promised date. If a contractor is paid late, the issue is the pay-run, not a variable earnings balance.


03


## What should stay the same on both runs?


Screening and the record. Whether you are paying a thousand creators or fifty contractors, an instruction that has not been screened should not move funds. If one recipient is flagged, that payout should be held for human review without freezing everyone else.[Mass payouts at network scale](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/insights/mass-payouts-at-network-scale) is the argument for why shared vetting, not raw volume, is what lets a run scale.


The close should also look the same: one reconciled report across corridors, so finance is not stitching together a chain explorer, a bank file, and a spreadsheet.[Global Mass Payouts](https://infinite.net/solutions/global-mass-payouts) is the shared product surface.


04


## How should you choose rails for each run?


The same way, per corridor: what the recipient can receive, and when the funds must be final. Creators can be paid to local accounts where the corridor supports it, or in stablecoins. Contractors can as well.[Transfer Routes](https://infinite.net/platform/transfer-routes) picks the rail; the[coverage list](https://infinite.net/resources/coverage) is the source for available markets. Do not assume every creator wants a stablecoin, and do not assume every contractor can only take a wire.


05


## When does a platform need both?


When it pays employees or contractors on a schedule and also pays creators when they earn. Those should be separate runs, even if they share an account and an API. Mixing a payroll roster with a variable creator batch makes failures and exceptions harder to explain. Keep the rails and the screening common; keep the batches distinct.


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Can creator payouts and contractor payroll share the same account?


Yes, they can share an account, an API, and the same screening. They should still be submitted as separate runs, because the cadence, the amounts, and the exception handling are different.


### Are creators screened the same way as contractors?


Each recipient is reviewed before the first payment, and each payout instruction is screened before funds move. A creator who earns occasionally is not exempt from that, and a contractor on a regular schedule is not reviewed only once for all future pay-runs.


### What happens if one creator payout in a batch fails?


The failed payout should be reported with its reason, and the rest of the run should continue. You can correct the destination or the details and resend that payout alone, instead of rolling back the batch.
